meta.title: Learning Anywhere
meta.description: SIDE is a K-12 online public school in Western Australia, supporting students wherever they are.

frames.title: Learning Anywhere
frames.body: Our partner schools support students whose learning journeys don’t follow a single pathway. Across metropolitan, regional, and remote WA, these schools provide continuity for students managing travel, training commitments, health needs, or changing circumstances — ensuring access to education that adapts while remaining connected to local communities.

sections.title: Hello, it’s good to see you!
sections.body:
Founded in 1918 as the Correspondence School, SIDE has built a proud tradition of student success across all years. Our dedicated staff deliver high-quality, tailored learning experiences to students regardless of their circumstances or location.

In K-6, we partner closely with parents to support foundational learning, while in Years 7-12 we foster growing independence and collaborate with student supervisors to guide each learner’s journey.

We maintain strong relationships with parents, carers, schools, student supervisors and the wider community — welcoming visits to our Leederville campus and prioritizing open, positive communication.

SIDE offers the same broad educational opportunities as traditional schools, including specialized support for students with disabilities, learning difficulties, or gifted and talented needs.

**Welcome to the School of Isolated and Distance Education!**

sections.title: What We Offer
sections.text: Everyone deserves access to quality education. Whether living in a remote location, balancing travel commitments, or managing health challenges, SIDE enables people to continue learning no matter what their unique situation might be.

frames.title: Home-based
frames.body: Students can complete their studies from home through scheduled online classes, independent learning tasks, and ongoing teacher guidance.

frames.title: School-based
frames.body: We partner with schools to deliver subjects that may not be available locally. Students remain connected to their enrolling school while accessing lessons taught by SIDE.

frames.title: Blended
frames.body: Secondary students can combine school-based attendance with online lessons. This option supports students engaged in high intensity athletic or artistic pursuits.

sections.title: SIDE Graduate Alex Saffy takes the bronze in the 2024 Paralympic Games.
sections.body:
Dubbed by fans and friends as the ‘Bunbury Bullet’, SIDE graduate Alex Saffy secured the bronze medal in the Men’s 100m butterfly S10 at the 2024 Paralympic Games in Paris, delivering a performance that also established a new Oceania record.

Competing against an international field, his race reflected years of structured training, technical refinement, and competitive consistency at the highest level of para-swimming.

As part of SIDE’s Elite Performance Program, Alex was able to prioritise his demanding training schedule while continuing his academic studies in parallel. The program’s flexible delivery allowed him to balance national and international competition commitments with coursework, ultimately enabling him to complete and achieve his WACE certification alongside his sporting career.

sections.title: Dancers following their dreams.
sections.body:
The SCSA-endorsed Community Arts Program at SIDE supports aspiring dancers in developing their artistic practice while continuing to engage in a structured and recognised secondary education pathway. Students are able to commit to regular training, rehearsals, and performance opportunities without compromising their academic responsibilities.

Through a balance of creative exploration and disciplined technique, the program prepares students for the practical demands of the performing arts industry. Participants build foundational skills in collaboration, self-management, and performance readiness, equipping them to progress toward further training or professional pathways in dance and related creative fields.

sections.title: We’ve joined with over 287 schools across WA
sections.alt: A tilted map of Western Australia with markers showing where SIDE’s partner schools are, concentrated around Perth, the South West and Wheatbelt, with others spread across the Mid West, Goldfields, Pilbara and Kimberley.
sections.body:
From the Wheatbelt to The Kimberley, each partnership represents an active connection — coordinated delivery, shared planning, and local adaptation that cares about the culture of the region.

Together, these schools form a distributed network that supports learning across metropolitan, regional, and remote communities that provide a diverse range of unique strengths:

items: Schools across WA are able to extend learning beyond the limits of a single campus
Distance and location don’t prevent students from accessing structured learning
Schooling can move with students across home, travel, and local communities
